title: Optimize native Round2 order resource
objective: Profile and optimize the shared FLINT/GMP native Round2 order resource for PARI regressions 2510 and 1710 to within 2x and then 1.25 geometric mean without changing the mathematical algorithm

oracles: ordinary Python Round2 exact local HNF
direct PARI and Hecke hard-case references
exceptions: Existing audited shared FLINT/GMP representation primitive only; no new handwritten mathematical algorithm

handoff.summary: Optimized the existing shared Zassenhaus Round-2 resource without changing its mathematical algorithm. The hard-case medians fell from 1989.901 to 373.284 microseconds for PARI #2510 and from 5523.624 to 1015.344 microseconds for #1710. Both are within 2x of the faster direct reference and the geometric-mean ratio is 1.102. Exact frozen payloads, an exact lattice-inverse differential, 32 deterministic randomized differentials, lifecycle stress, ASan/UBSan, the full build, and the Round-4 agreement suite pass.
risks: The checked sparse word accumulator is enabled only where __int128 is available; native Windows x64 keeps the tested exact packed-fmpz transform fallback until a portable checked double-limb accumulator is added and benchmarked.

architecture/native-audit.json still records the old 502-line/18889-byte audit metrics and old rational-transform wording for number_field_order_ffi.h; the integration lane must refresh it to 1077 lines/43540 bytes and review the updated packed-integer/p^2 responsibilities.
next_steps: Integration lane: refresh the number_field_order_ffi.h entry in architecture/native-audit.json, then run pnpm architecture:check.
Integration lane: rerun the focused Windows lifecycle witness; exact fallback is exercised by SAGEJS_NF_ORDER_FORCE_EXACT_MULTIPLIER on Unix and remains the Windows path.
Use bench/results/number-field-round2-resource-2026-08-18.json as the Milestone 3 performance receipt.
